questions.question: Which feature of NHS-crosslinked heparin affected FGF2-array signal relative to non-crosslinked heparin?

options.C: It produced equal signal but only at 48 h.

questions.rationale: Both formats bound FGF2 dose-dependently, but covalent NHS coupling markedly improved retained/displayed signal.
questions.evidence_quote: Both immobilization strategies resulted in a dose-dependent FGF2 binding, with the NHScrosslinked heparin providing ~ 5-to 10-fold higher signal.

questions.question: After 48 h under culture conditions, what fraction of FGF2-binding activity remained on the arrays?

options.A: About 40%, following an initial decrease during the first 18 h.
options.B: About 90%, following an initial rise during the first 18 h.
options.C: About 15%, with all loss occurring in the first hour.

questions.rationale: The heparin remained relatively stable after the early decrease and retained around two-fifths of FGF2-binding activity at 48 hours.
questions.evidence_quote: Over this time, the arrays were probed with FGF2-AF647 to assess heparin retention (Figure 2B ) After an initial decrease in binding activity during the first 18 hours, the heparin arrays remained stable with ~ 40% of FGF2 binding activity being retained after 48 hours.

questions.question: Which sulfation pattern produced the strongest FGF2 binding, and what happened as sulfate groups were removed?

options.A: Fully sulfated heparin bound most strongly; removal of 6-O-, 2-O-, and N-sulfates progressively reduced activity.
options.B: N-desulfated heparin bound most strongly; removing 2-O-sulfate increased binding.
options.C: All derivatives bound equally, showing sulfation was irrelevant.

questions.rationale: The array preserved structure-dependent recognition: fully sulfated heparin was preferred and desulfation progressively impaired activity.
questions.evidence_quote: FGF2 bound most strongly to the fully sulfated heparin. Removal of 6-O-, 2-O-and N-sulfates resulted in progressive loss of activity, which is in agreement with the known requirements of 2-O-and N-sulfation for FGF2 binding to HS.

questions.question: Why were Ext1−/− embryonic stem cells selected for the signaling assay?

options.A: They lack cell-surface HS and thus isolate the contribution of arrayed GAGs from endogenous HS.
options.B: They overproduce HS and amplify endogenous FGF2 signaling.
options.C: They cannot express FGF receptors, providing a negative control for cell adhesion.
options.D: They differentiate spontaneously into neural cells on gelatin.

questions.rationale: Ext1 is needed for HS chain assembly; the mutant cells lack endogenous surface HS and are unable to engage HS-dependent factors such as FGF2.
questions.evidence_quote: In the absence of this enzyme, the Ext1 -/-ESCs lack cell surface HS structures and are unable to engage a range of HSdependent GFs, [26] including FGF2. As such, these mutant ECS are ideally suited to isolate the effects of the arrayed GAGs on FGF2 signaling from those of endogenous HS structures.

questions.question: Which seeding density produced consistent ESC monolayers, and why were the two extremes unsuitable?

options.A: 40,000 cells/cm²; 20,000 grew slowly/irregularly while 100,000 caused overgrowth and detachment.
options.C: 100,000 cells/cm²; lower densities failed to attach.
options.D: 500,000 cells/cm²; both smaller densities caused detachment.

questions.rationale: An intermediate density balanced adequate colony growth against spot overgrowth and cell loss.
questions.evidence_quote: While seeding the stem cells too sparsely (20,000 cells/cm 2 ) resulted in slow growth and irregular colony formation, too high seeding density (100,000 cells/cm 2 ) led to rapid proliferation resulting in spot overgrowth and cell detachment. The intermediary seeding density (40,000 cells/cm 2 ) produced consistent monolayers of Ext1 -/- ESCs

questions.question: Under what FGF2 stimulation conditions did the authors measure array-based ERK activation?

options.C: 0.5 µg/mL for 15 h at room temperature.

questions.rationale: The cellular readout followed a 15-minute stimulation with 0.5 ng/mL FGF2 at physiological temperature.
questions.evidence_quote: The cells were then placed in a fresh serum-free media containing FGF2 (0.5 ng/mL) and stimulated for 15 min at 37 C.

questions.question: Which conditions increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation in Ext1−/− ESCs, compared with gelatin alone?

options.A: FGF2 together with immobilized heparin or soluble heparin.
options.C: Gelatin alone or FGF2 without heparin.
options.D: NHS reagent alone, with or without FGF2.

questions.rationale: The cells required FGF2 plus either arrayed or soluble heparin for significant pERK induction.
questions.evidence_quote: While ERK1/2 protein levels were similar across all conditions, only Ext1 -/-ESCs stimulated with FGF2 in the presence of immobilized or soluble heparin showed significant increase in Erk1/2 phosphorylation

questions.question: How did arrayed-heparin MAPK activity compare with soluble heparin, and what explanation was proposed?

options.A: Arrayed heparin gave somewhat lower activity, possibly because it was accessible to only a subset of FGFRs at cell contact points.
options.B: Arrayed heparin gave higher activity because it reached all FGFRs.
options.C: The signals were identical because immobilization had no effect.
options.D: Arrayed heparin suppressed phosphorylation by blocking all receptor access.

questions.rationale: The authors observed a lower array signal and suggested restricted spatial accessibility of immobilized glycans as a possible explanation.
questions.evidence_quote: We observed somewhat lower levels of MAPK activity on the arrayed heparin compared to its soluble form (Figure 4B ). This may be due to the a more limited accessibility of the immobilized heparin to only a subset of FGFRs localized to the point of cell contact with the array.

questions.question: What was the effect of increasing immobilized heparin concentration from 0 to 500 µg/mL during FGF2 stimulation?

options.A: ERK1/2 phosphorylation increased in a heparin dose-responsive manner.
options.C: No signaling response occurred at any concentration.
options.D: Signaling increased only at zero heparin.

questions.rationale: The study reports a concentration-dependent signaling response across the immobilized heparin series.
questions.evidence_quote: showed a heparin doseresponsive ERK1/2 phosphorylation

questions.question: What methodological advantage was gained by NHS-crosslinking GAGs to gelatin in the hydrogel array?

options.A: Retention during culture improved without detectable alteration of polysaccharide protein-binding specificity.
options.B: It made all GAGs bind FGF2 equally, eliminating selectivity.
options.C: It converted the hydrogel into a nonadhesive cell-repellent surface.
options.D: It replaced the need for growth-factor stimulation.

questions.rationale: The authors conclude that crosslinking improves display stability while preserving recognition properties, enabling cellular signaling measurements.
questions.evidence_quote: The crosslinking facilitated the retention of the polysaccharides on the array during cell culture without altering the protein-binding specificity of the polysaccharides.
